payload.analysis: Current evidence strongly supports metastatic carcinoma causing cholestatic liver injury: markedly elevated ALP/GGT with mild transaminases, hilar irregular isoechoic mass on ultrasound, and PAX8-positive malignant cells with bile duct destruction on biopsy. This explains persistent enzyme elevation despite stopping alcohol and axitinib, effectively ruling out drug-induced injury and primary biliary disease. However, the primary site remains unidentified due to missing PET-CT and full immunohistochemistry panel; despite retrieval limits, all currently available key information has been integrated and the leading hypothesis is confirmed.

payload.analysis: Based on current evidence, markedly elevated ALP and GGT with relatively mild transaminases indicate a cholestatic process. Ultrasound shows an irregular isoechoic region at the hepatic hilum, and biopsy confirms PAX8-positive malignant cells with bile duct destruction, strongly supporting metastatic carcinoma as the cause. Although MRCP and bilirubin levels remain unavailable, the combination of imaging and histology covers the key diagnostic information, effectively ruling out drug-induced and chronic liver disease. Clinical correlation and management for metastatic carcinoma are recommended.

payload.report: Markedly elevated ALP/GGT with mild transaminases indicates cholestasis. Ultrasound/MRI localize to hepatic hilum. Biopsy showing PAX8-positive malignant cells with bile duct destruction is gold-standard for metastatic carcinoma, explaining secondary cholestatic injury. Enzymes remained elevated despite stopping alcohol/axitinib; viral/autoimmune/metabolic liver disease absent, excluding drug-induced and chronic liver disease. Thus metastatic carcinoma at hepatic hilum is the cause.
